We’re often impressed by people with exceptional memory. That’s why memory games are so popular, and that’s exactly what you’re going to build!

     

Your Memory game will follow a typical flow.

   


Let's build the FIRST TWO PARTS:

1. Add New Colour to List

  • Start with an empty list.
  • Each round, add one random colour to the list (red, orange, green, or blue).

2. Show List of Colours

  • Display the colours in the list one by one, in order.

3.The program continues to run, adding one new colour to the list each round. Follow the display format below.

You can also remove an item as shown. If you try to remove value at an invalid index or when the list is empty, the program will crash.

1. Add New Colour to List

  • Start with an empty list.
  • Each round, add one random colour to the list (red, orange, green, or blue).

2. Show List of Colours

  • Display the colours in the list one by one, in order.

3. Select Colour in Sequence

  • Prompt the user to choose the next colour in the sequence (the number is shown).
  • Press Button D18 to confirm the selection.

      
4. Check Answer

  • Compare the selected colour to the colour in the list (at the right index).
  • If they match, display "right" for a second and repeat from Step (1) to add another colour and continue.
  • If they do not match, display "wrong" for a second, then clear the list and restart the game from Step (1).
